item.title: Catherine O’Hara, Iconic ‘Home Alone’ and ‘Schitt’s Creek’ Star, Dead at 71
item.description: The beloved comic actress from Canada won Emmys for the more recent "Schitt's Creek" and for her role on the sketch series "SCTV" in the 1980s.

item.title: Hot Off Their Oscar Noms, ‘Sinners’ and ‘Sentimental Value’ Stars Round Out SBIFF Virtuosos Tribute
item.description: Exclusive: Oscar nominees Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas and Wunmi Mosaku will join this year's star-studded Virtuosos tribute. Oscar nominees Delroy Lindo and Jerry Bruckheimer will also have festival events.

item.title: Riz Ahmed Has Never Auditioned for Bond, but His Show ‘Bait’ Is a Chance to Throw Himself in the Mix
item.description: "Bait" creator/star Riz Ahmed and his co-star Guz Khan spoke at the IndieWire Studio at Sundance, presented by Dropbox, about their new industry satire "Bait," premiering on Amazon in March.

item.title: Another Messy Awards Season? How the California Post’s Safdies Cover Story Could Impact ‘Marty Supreme’ Oscar Chances
item.description: Plus: "Screen Talk" co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio discuss Sundance and welcome Santa Barbara Film Festival director Roger Durling to the podcast.

item.title: Highlighted by Nicole Holofcener, the Sundance Episodic Series Refuse to Judge How We Live in 2026
item.description: Sundance's 2026 TV section features a gem of a pilot from the "Enough Said" director, a gripping documentary about the art world's "trial of the century," and a lot of people who are really going through it, just like the rest of us.

item.title: Martin Scorsese Remembers Catherine O’Hara: ‘A True Artist, and a Wonderful Human Being’
item.description: The Emmy-winning comic actress died unexpectedly on January 30 at the age of 71. Scorsese directed her in his 1985 film "After Hours."

item.title: Sundance’s ‘Take Me Home’ Turned a Personal Story Into an Anti-Ableist Creative Undertaking
item.description: Liz Sargent directs her sister Anna Sargent, who has cognitive disability, in a film that started as a Sundance short. They spoke, along with co-star Ali Ahn, about the project at IndieWire's Sundance Studio, presented by Dropbox.

item.title: Sundance 2026 Movies Sold So Far: Stephanie Ahn’s ‘Bedford Park’ Sells to Sony Pictures Classics
item.description: Moon Choi and Son Sukku star in this drama about a Korean American woman grappling with her cultural past.

item.title: Lav Diaz on ‘Magellan,’ His NYFF Joke About Casting Gael García Bernal During Sex, and Béla Tarr’s Stubborn Nature
item.description: Filipino auteur Diaz and his star García Bernal tell IndieWire about everything that went into playing Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan — and the portrayal by a Mexican actor.

item.title: Are You Scared of the U.S. Government Turning on Its Own Citizens? Try 1971’s ‘Punishment Park’
item.description: Peter Watkins' controversial anti-war film is brutal to watch, but its terrifying themes haven't aged a day.
